facts.text: I have been playing guitar for about three months.
I am getting more comfortable with basic chords like G, C, and D.
I recently played my first full song, "Sweet Child O' Mine".
I am interested in learning "Wonderwall" by Oasis.
I have been experimenting with open D tuning.
I am using a new Taylor GS Mini guitar.
I have been taking guitar lessons for the past three months.
My guitar instructor is Alex.
I meet with Alex every Wednesday evening at 7 pm.
I am thinking of recording myself playing "Wonderwall".
I plan to share the recording with my music meetup group.
I have a question about recording my guitar in open D tuning on my Taylor GS Mini.
I am considering using a microphone more sensitive to midrange frequencies to capture warmth and resonance.
I am considering whether a microphone with a more balanced frequency response would work as well.
I think I will use a dynamic microphone like the Shure SM57.
I have heard great things about the Shure SM57.
The Shure SM57 is known for midrange emphasis.
I believe the midrange emphasis should help bring out the full-bodied sound of my guitar.
I think the Shure SM57 is an affordable option.
I want to experiment with different microphone placements to find the sweet spot for my guitar.
